mainTopic: When a גוי's possible contact makes a Jew's wine forbidden as יין נסך: fear of being seen, following the majority, and ספק ספיקא
overview: This amud is about wine belonging to a Jew that a גוי may have touched, which would make it forbidden as יין נסך. It opens by finishing a case: a respectable Jewish woman dining with גוים keeps her wine permitted, but a זונה's wine is forbidden because the גוים do not respect her. Then רבא rules on a long series of real-life stories: a גוי locked in a wine room with a crack in the door, a quarrel outside, a גוי found at an inn or in a house, a Jew who left to daven or to keep שבת, and a גוי hiding from a lion. The idea running through them is that a גוי who fears being seen or caught will not pour a libation, so the wine stays permitted. A ברייתא is used to challenge one ruling, and the גמרא answers by narrowing it to a גוי who has an excuse for being there. The story of איסור גיורא shows that non-Jews believed Jews would break שבת for money, so the גוי on the boat still expects the Jew back. Finally, רבא and שמואל permit wine opened by thieves. רבא's reason is that most thieves there are Jews. The גמרא asks if שמואל follows רבי אליעזר's rule about a doubtful entry, then answers that the wine case is a ספק ספיקא.

steps.title: Their desire for libation wine is not strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why a Jewish woman's wine stays permitted when she dines with גוים: they do not have a strong urge to make יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: The urge to pour wine as a libation is not strong for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a reason that started just before this section. That reason explained why a respectable Jewish woman eating with גוים does not lose her wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the גוים will not go against her wishes just to pour a libation, because that urge is weak for them. So they will not touch her wine for עבודה זרה, and it stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: wine poured or set aside as an offering to עבודה זרה

phrases.english: The urge for libation wine
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that began earlier, about a Jewish woman eating with גוים.

phrases.english: is not strong for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִצְרָא דְּיֵין נֶסֶךְ לָא תָּקֵיף לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of the previous case, which started before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גוים will not pour a libation from a respected Jewish woman's wine against her will, because their urge for יין נסך is weak.

steps.title: A Jewish prostitute dining with gentiles: the wine is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Unlike the respectable woman, a Jewish זונה eating with גוים has her wine forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a Jewish prostitute is eating together with gentiles, the wine is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a contrasting case: a Jewish זונה at the table with גוים. Here the wine is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup is almost the same as the last case: a Jewish woman and גוים eating together. But the ruling flips, which tells us that something about who she is makes the difference. The גמרא will explain this next.

phrases.english: A Jewish prostitute and gentiles dining together
the wine is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית וְגוֹיִם מְסוּבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the respectable woman's case and gives the opposite ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a Jewish זונה dines with גוים, the wine is forbidden.

steps.title: Why is her wine forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the different ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the זונה's wine is forbidden when the other woman's wine was permitted. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both women are Jewish and both are eating with גוים. So the גמרא wants to know exactly what makes the difference.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the זונה's case is different from the respectable woman's case.

steps.title: She is not respected, so she goes along with them
steps.stepSummary: Because the גוים look down on her, she gives in to them, and they will pour the wine without caring what she thinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since she is cheap in their eyes, she is pulled along after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the גוים have no respect for a זונה. So she cannot stop them, and they will do what they want with the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the respectable woman, the גוים respect her wishes and their urge for יין נסך is weak, so they hold back. With the זונה there is no such respect, so nothing holds them back. The difference is her standing in their eyes, not how strong their urge is.
steps.whatToRemember: A respectable Jewish woman's wine stays permitted at a table with גוים. A זונה's wine is forbidden, because they do not respect her and she follows their lead.

phrases.english: Since she is cheap in their eyes,
she is pulled along after them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְזִילָה עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גוים look down on her, so she gives in to them and they use the wine for libation without caring about her.

steps.title: Story: a gentile locked inside a wine room with a crack in the door
steps.stepSummary: A גוי went into a house where Jewish wine was stored and locked the door. There was a crack in the door, and he was found standing among the barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a house where a Jew's wine was kept. A gentile went in and locked the door in the Jew's face. There was a crack in the door, and the gentile was found standing between the barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story to set up a ruling by רבא. The question is whether the barrels became forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Locking himself in alone with the wine looks bad, because he could have poured a libation. But the crack in the door means someone could have seen him from outside. That detail will matter for the ruling.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא בֵּיתָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּיהּ חַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: There was a certain house in which a Jew's wine was kept.
A gentile went in and locked the door in his face.
phrases.notes: "His face" means the Jew's: the גוי shut the Jew out.

phrases.english: And there was a crack in the door.
The gentile was found standing among the barrels.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא בֵּיתָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּיהּ חַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of case stories about a גוי left alone with Jewish wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case. The ruling comes in the next step.

steps.title: רבא: barrels facing the crack are permitted, the others are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that barrels in view of the crack stay permitted, but barrels off to the sides are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: every barrel opposite the crack is permitted. The ones on this side and that side are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his ruling on the story, splitting the barrels into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי would be afraid to touch barrels that someone could see through the crack, so those stay permitted. Barrels outside that line of sight could have been used for a libation without anyone seeing, so they are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for the whole series: what matters is whether the גוי feared being seen.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רָבָא: כֹּל דְּלַהֲדֵי בִּיזְעָא — שְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: Rava said: all that are opposite the crack are permitted.
Those on this side and that side are forbidden.
phrases.notes: He means the barrels off to either side, which could not be seen through the crack.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: כֹּל דְּלַהֲדֵי בִּיזְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the story in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Barrels visible through the crack are permitted. Barrels out of view are forbidden.

steps.title: Story: a quarrel outside, and the gentile comes back first
steps.stepSummary: A Jew lived upstairs and a גוי downstairs, where Jewish wine was stored. Both went out at the sound of a fight. The גוי came back first and locked the door on the Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a Jew's wine kept in a house where a Jew lived upstairs and a gentile downstairs. They heard the sound of a fight and went out. The gentile came back first and locked the door in the Jew's face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story to set up another ruling by רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the Jew upstairs could keep an eye on the wine below. Here the גוי got back first and locked himself in, so it looks like he had a private chance to pour the wine.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא חַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּבֵיתָא,
phrases.english: There was a certain Jew's wine that was kept in a house

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה דָּיַיר יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה וְגוֹי בַּתַּחְתּוֹנָה.
phrases.english: where a Jew lived on the upper floor and a gentile on the lower floor.
They heard the sound of a fight and went out.

phrases.aramaic: קְדֵים אֲתָא גּוֹי אַחְדַּהּ לְדַשָּׁא בְּאַפֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: The gentile came back first and locked the door in his face.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא חַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּבֵיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case story on the same theme as step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case. The ruling comes next.

steps.title: רבא: permitted, because the gentile fears the Jew is already upstairs
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits the wine. The גוי would think: just as I got back early, maybe the Jew did too and is watching me from upstairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the wine is permitted. The gentile says to himself: just as I came back early, maybe the Jew also came back early, is sitting upstairs, and is watching me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules the wine permitted and explains what the גוי would be thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the door was locked, the גוי cannot be sure that no one is watching him from upstairs. Since he cannot be sure, he would be too afraid to pour the wine. The fear of possibly being seen is enough.

phrases.english: Rava said: the wine is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: מֵימָר אָמַר: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּקְדֵים אֲתַאי אֲנָא,
phrases.english: He says to himself: just as I came back early,
maybe the Jew came back early and is sitting upstairs
and is watching me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: חַמְרָא שְׁרֵי, מֵימָר אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling and reason for the story in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine is permitted, because the גוי fears the Jew may already be upstairs watching him.

steps.title: Story: a gentile found sitting among the barrels at an inn
steps.stepSummary: At an inn where Jewish wine was stored, a גוי was found sitting among the barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an inn where a Jew's wine was kept, and a gentile was found sitting among the barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a third story to set up another ruling by רבא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time nobody locked a door. The גוי was simply found there, and the question is how to judge why he was among the barrels.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּיהּ חַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: There was a certain inn in which a Jew's wine was kept.

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתְּכַח גּוֹי דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּי דַנֵּי.
phrases.english: A gentile was found sitting among the barrels.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּיהּ חַמְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third case story on the same theme.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case. The ruling comes next.

steps.title: רבא: if he acted like a caught thief, the wine is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the גוי reacted like a thief who got caught, the wine is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if he was caught there like a thief, the wine is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes the ruling depend on how the גוי reacted when he was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he acted startled and guilty, like a thief, he was scared of being caught, so he would not have dared to pour a libation. If he was calm and at ease, he felt free there, so the wine is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: caught like a thief: acting startled and guilty

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that a גוי acting "like a thief" makes the wine permitted. The reason is that someone afraid of being caught is too nervous to pour wine for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's stories so far the rule is the same: if the גוי feared being seen or caught, he would not pour a libation, so the wine stays permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רָבָא: אִם נִתְפָּס עָלָיו כְּגַנָּב — שְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: Rava said: if he was caught on it like a thief, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: He means the גוי looked startled and had no good excuse for being there.

phrases.english: And if not, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: אִם נִתְפָּס עָלָיו כְּגַנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the story in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the גוי acted like a thief who was caught, the wine is permitted. Otherwise it is forbidden.

steps.title: A gentile found standing among the wine barrels in a house
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a גוי is found standing among the barrels in a house where Jewish wine is stored.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a house where wine was stored, and a גוי was found standing among the barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new story so that רבא can rule on it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is close to the inn case in Step 9, but now it is a private house. The question is whether the wine became forbidden because the גוי may have touched it.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא בֵּיתָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּיהּ חַמְרָא,
phrases.english: There was a certain house in which wine was stored,

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתְּכַח גּוֹי דַּהֲוָה קָאֵים בֵּי דַנֵּי.
phrases.english: a גוי was found standing among the barrels.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא בֵּיתָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּיהּ חַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case like the inn case of Steps 9-10, now set in a house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a גוי found among the barrels in a house.

steps.title: If the gentile has an excuse ready, the wine is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules: if the גוי has a way to excuse his being there, the wine is forbidden. If he has none, the wine is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he has a way to excuse himself, the wine is forbidden. If not, the wine is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules on the house case. It all depends on whether the גוי had an excuse for being near the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי with an excuse ready is not afraid of getting caught, so he may have handled the wine freely. A גוי with no excuse would be scared to touch it, so we assume he did not. It is the same idea as Step 10: what decides the case is the גוי's fear of being caught.

keyTerms.meaning: To excuse himself, to have a pretext for being there

steps.confusionAlert: It feels backwards, but having an excuse makes the wine FORBIDDEN. The excuse takes away his fear, and fear is what protects the wine.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he has a way to excuse himself (for being there),
the wine is forbidden,
and if not, the wine is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: אִי אִית לֵיהּ לְאִישְׁתְּמוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case from Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי with an excuse for being there makes the wine forbidden. A גוי without one leaves it permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to forbid the wine even with no excuse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the inn was locked, or the Jew told the גוי to guard the wine, the wine is forbidden. It seems to say this even when the גוי has no excuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'If the inn was locked, or he told him "Guard it," it is forbidden.' Doesn't that mean even when the גוי has no excuse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא that seems to forbid the wine without making any exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids the wine in these cases and does not mention any excuse. That makes it look like the wine is forbidden even with no excuse, which goes against רבא's rule.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If the inn was locked (with the גוי inside),
or if he said to him "Guard it," it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ לְאִישְׁתְּמוֹטֵי?
phrases.english: Doesn't this mean even if he has no way to excuse himself?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that without an excuse the wine stays permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids the wine with no exception, which suggests it is forbidden even without an excuse.

steps.title: The ברייתא is talking about a gentile who has an excuse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the גוי does have an excuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about where he has a way to excuse himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא to one kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only forbids the wine when the גוי has an excuse for being there. So it agrees with רבא, and his rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he has

phrases.english: No, it is talking about where he does have a way to excuse himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בִּדְאִית לֵיהּ לְאִישְׁתְּמוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids the wine even when the גוי has no excuse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a גוי who has an excuse, which fits רבא's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: What decides these cases is whether the גוי is afraid of being caught. If he has an excuse, the wine is forbidden. If he has none, it stays permitted.

steps.title: A Jew leaves his wine to go daven
steps.stepSummary: A Jew and a גוי were drinking wine together. The Jew heard davening in the shul and got up and left.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew and a גוי were sitting and drinking wine. The Jew heard the sound of prayer in the shul, got up, and left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new story so that רבא can rule on it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the Jew left suddenly and the גוי was alone with the wine. Nobody told the גוי how long the Jew would be gone.

phrases.english: There was a certain Jew and a גוי
who were sitting and drinking wine.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל קָל צַלּוֹיֵי בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא,
phrases.english: The Jew heard the sound of prayer in the shul,
he got up and left.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹי דַּהֲווֹ יָתְבִי וְקָא שָׁתוּ חַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about a Jew who left his wine without warning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a Jew who left suddenly to daven.

steps.title: The wine stays permitted because the gentile expects him back
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits the wine. The גוי thinks the Jew will remember his wine and come right back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the wine is permitted. The גוי says to himself: any moment now he'll remember his wine and come back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules on the davening story and gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי expects the Jew to come back at any moment, so he is afraid to touch the wine. That fear keeps the wine permitted, just like the reasoning in Step 8.

phrases.english: Rava said: The wine is permitted,
because (the גוי) says to himself:

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא מִדְּכַר לֵיהּ לְחַמְרֵיהּ וְהָדַר אָתֵי.
phrases.english: Any moment now he'll remember his wine and come back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: חַמְרָא שְׁרֵי, מֵימָר אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on Step 15's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine is permitted because the גוי fears the Jew could come back at any moment.

steps.title: A Jew leaves the boat when the שופר announces שבת
steps.stepSummary: A Jew and a גוי were on a boat. The Jew heard the twilight שופר announcing שבת and got off.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew and a גוי were sitting on a boat. The Jew heard the sound of the twilight שופר, got off, and left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up another story so that רבא can rule on it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the Jew left because שבת was starting. That makes it seem less likely that he would come back soon.

keyTerms.meaning: The שופר blasts at twilight, announcing שבת

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹי דַּהֲווֹ יָתְבִי בְּאַרְבָּא,
phrases.english: There was a certain Jew and a גוי who were sitting on a boat.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל קָל שִׁיפּוּרֵי דְּבֵי שִׁימְשֵׁי,
phrases.english: The Jew heard the sound of the twilight שופר blasts,
he got off and left.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹי דַּהֲווֹ יָתְבִי בְּאַרְבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story where a Jew left suddenly, this time for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a Jew who left the boat as שבת began.

steps.title: Same ruling on the boat: the wine is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא again permits the wine, with the same reasoning: the גוי expects the Jew to come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the wine is permitted. The גוי says to himself: any moment now he'll remember his wine and come back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the same ruling and the same reason as in the davening story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the Jew left for שבת, רבא says the גוי still expects him to return for his wine. That fear keeps the wine permitted. The next step asks how this can be true on שבת.

phrases.english: Rava said: The wine is permitted,
because (the גוי) says to himself:

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא מִדְּכַר לֵיהּ לְחַמְרֵיהּ וְהָדַר אָתֵי.
phrases.english: Any moment now he'll remember his wine and come back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: חַמְרָא שְׁרֵי, מֵימָר אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on Step 17's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine on the boat stays permitted because the גוי fears the Jew will come back.

steps.title: But on שבת the Jew would not come back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a worry: the גוי knows the Jew is keeping שבת, so he would not expect him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: because of שבת (the גוי knows the Jew won't return)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible problem with רבא's boat ruling. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גוי knows that Jews don't travel or carry on שבת, he would feel safe being alone with the wine. Then there is no fear, and the wine should be forbidden.

phrases.english: And if you say (the גוי isn't worried) because of שבת,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִשּׁוּם שַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning of Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the גוי expects the Jew to return on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Jew keeping שבת would not come back, so the גוי has nothing to fear.

steps.title: איסור גיורא: gentiles thought Jews don't really keep שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that איסור גיורא said that before converting, he and other non-Jews believed Jews don't really keep שבת, because no wallets were ever left lying in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say: איסור the convert told me, when we were still non-Jews we used to say that Jews don't keep שבת, because if they did, so many wallets would be found lying in the market!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry by showing that non-Jews believed Jews would break שבת to get money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-Jews never saw lost wallets left lying around on שבת, so they figured Jews picked them up and carried them. So the גוי on the boat would think the Jew might come back for his valuable wine even on שבת. His fear stays, and the wine stays permitted.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
Issur the convert told me:
When we were still non-Jews,
we used to say: Jews don't keep שבת,
for if they kept שבת,
how many wallets would be found (lying) in the market!
phrases.notes: His point: on שבת no lost wallets were ever left lying around, so it looked like Jews were picking them up.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמַר רָבָא: אֲמַר לִי אִיסּוּר גִּיּוֹרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing what the גוי actually believes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גוי assumes the Jew won't return on שבת, so he has no fear.
steps.terutzMaskana: Non-Jews believed Jews would break שבת for money, so the גוי still fears the Jew may return.

steps.title: Why the wallets disappeared: the rule of רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: איסור explains that he didn't know Jews hold like רבי יצחק, who allows moving a found wallet on שבת in stretches of less than ד' אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I didn't know that we hold like רבי יצחק, who said: one who finds a wallet on שבת may move it along, less than four אמות at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: איסור finishes his story by explaining what non-Jews misunderstood about the missing wallets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wallets disappeared because Jews moved them in a way that is allowed, not because they broke שבת. But the non-Jews didn't know this. So a גוי really does think a Jew might break שבת for his property, and that is why רבא's reasoning holds.

keyTerms.meaning: In stretches, each less than four אמות

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי who thinks the Jew might come back to his wine is afraid to touch it, so the wine stays permitted. This holds even on שבת, because non-Jews thought Jews would break שבת for money.

phrases.english: And I didn't know
that we hold like Rabbi Yitzchak,
for Rabbi Yitzchak said:
One who finds a wallet on שבת
may carry it along, less than four אמות at a time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא דִּסְבִירָא לַן כְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes איסור's story from Step 20 by explaining the real reason the wallets disappeared.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק: a wallet found on שבת may be moved in stretches of less than four אמות.

steps.title: A frightened גוי hides among the wine barrels
steps.stepSummary: A lion roared in a winepress, and a גוי who heard it hid among the wine barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a lion roaring in a winepress. A גוי heard it and hid among the barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story that sets up רבא's ruling in the next step. A scared גוי ends up alone among barrels of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being alone with wine usually raises the worry that the גוי touched it and made it forbidden. Here he did not come to the wine on purpose; he ran there to hide. The next step asks whether the wine is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A winepress, where grapes are pressed into wine

phrases.english: There was a certain lion that was roaring in a winepress.
A gentile heard it,
and he hid among the barrels.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא אַרְיָא דַּהֲוָה נָהֵים בְּמַעְצַרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the boat case (steps 17-21), the גמרא brings another case of a גוי left alone with wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case: a גוי hid among wine barrels out of fear of a lion.

steps.title: רבא permits the wine because the גוי feared being watched
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits the wine. The גוי thought that just as he was hiding, a Jew might be hiding behind him and watching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wine is permitted. The גוי tells himself: Just as I am hiding, a Jew may also be hiding behind me and watching me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules on the lion case and permits the wine. His reason is that the גוי was afraid someone might see him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic matches the earlier cases: if the גוי fears a Jew might see him, he will not dare touch the wine. Here the fear comes from the hiding itself. Since he knows he is hiding, he assumes a Jew could be hiding nearby too.

keyTerms.meaning: He says to himself; he would think

phrases.english: Rava said: The wine is permitted,
because he says to himself:
Just as I am hiding,
a Jew may also be hiding behind me
and watching me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: חַמְרָא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's ruling on the lion case from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine is permitted, because a גוי who is hiding fears that a Jew may be hiding nearby and watching him, so he will not touch the wine.

steps.title: Thieves open barrels in פומבדיתא and רבא permits the wine
steps.stepSummary: Thieves came to פומבדיתא and opened many wine barrels. רבא permits the wine because most thieves there are Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some thieves came to פומבדיתא and opened many barrels. רבא said: The wine is permitted. Why? Most of the thieves are Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case of thieves opening wine barrels. רבא permits the wine and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know who these thieves were. רבא follows the majority (רוב): most thieves in פומבדיתא are Jewish, so we assume these were too, and the wine stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Jewish city in בבל

phrases.english: There were certain thieves who came to Pumbedita
and opened many barrels.
Rava said: The wine is permitted.
What is the reason?
Most of the thieves are Jews.
phrases.notes: He means most of the thieves in פומבדיתא, so we assume these ones were Jewish too.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ גַּנָּבֵי דְּסָלְקִי לְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case of possible גוי contact with wine, solved by following the majority instead of the 'fear of being seen' reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine is permitted because most thieves in פומבדיתא are Jewish, and we follow the majority.

steps.title: A similar case in נהרדעא, and שמואל permits
steps.stepSummary: A similar thing happened in נהרדעא, and שמואל also said the wine is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident in נהרדעא, and שמואל said: The wine is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that שמואל ruled the same way in a similar case in נהרדעא. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל permits the wine, but no reason is given. Without the reason of 'most thieves are Jewish', the גמרא will now ask which opinion his ruling depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident; a case that happened
נהרדעא, the city where שמואל lived and taught

phrases.english: There was an incident in Neharde'a,
and Shmuel said: The wine is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to רבא's case in פומבדיתא, with the same outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the נהרדעא thieves case, the wine is permitted.

steps.title: Whose opinion does שמואל follow? Perhaps רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view שמואל's ruling matches, and suggests רבי אליעזר, who holds that a doubt about entering a place stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It seems to follow רבי אליעזר, who says: If there is a doubt whether someone entered, he is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא שמואל's ruling depends on. It suggests רבי אליעזר's rule about a ספק ביאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that in נהרדעא the real doubt is whether a גוי thief ever got to the wine at all. That looks like רבי אליעזר's rule: if we are unsure whether a person entered a place of טומאה, we say he is טהור. Tying שמואל to one specific תנא suggests that others may not agree.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
A doubt whether someone entered (a certain place)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר's rule is about טומאה (ritual impurity), not wine. The גמרא is only borrowing his logic about a doubt whether someone entered, and applying it to whether a גוי reached the wine.

phrases.english: In accordance with whose opinion is this?
It follows Rabbi Eliezer, who says:
If there is a doubt about entering, he is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source behind שמואל's ruling in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view is the basis for שמואל permitting the wine in נהרדעא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The suggestion is רבי אליעזר, who rules that a ספק ביאה is טהור.

steps.title: The משנה where רבי אליעזר rules on a doubtful entry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a man who walked through a valley in the rainy season. רבי אליעזר says a doubt about entering is טהור, but a doubt about touching is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Someone went into a valley during the rainy season, and there was טומאה in a certain field. He says: I walked in that area, but I don't know if I went into that field or not. רבי אליעזר says: A doubt about entering is טהור; a doubt about touching is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that is the source for רבי אליעזר's rule from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר makes a split. If we don't know whether the man even entered the field, he is טהור. But if he surely entered and we only doubt whether he touched the טומאה, he is טמא. The גמרא compares שמואל's case to the first half: a doubt whether the גוי ever reached the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: A valley; an open field area
A doubt whether someone touched (the טומאה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: doubt whether you entered the place = טהור; doubt whether you touched the טומאה = טמא. The גמרא suggests שמואל's wine ruling relies on the first half of this rule.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
One who enters a valley during the rainy season,
and there was impurity in a certain field,
and he said: I walked in that area,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם נִכְנַסְתִּי לְאוֹתָהּ שָׂדֶה
phrases.english: but I do not know whether I entered that field
or whether I did not enter it,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
If the doubt is about entering, he is pure;
if the doubt is about touching, he is impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַנִּכְנָס לְבִקְעָה בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה behind רבי אליעזר's rule that step 26 tied to שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds a ספק ביאה is טהור, the rule step 26 suggested as the basis for שמואל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in טהרות 6:5 (the man in the valley during the rainy season).

steps.title: The wine case is different because it is a double doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that שמואל must follow רבי אליעזר. In the case of the thieves, some thieves open barrels looking for money, so there are two doubts, a ספק ספיקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case there is different. Since some thieves open barrels to look for money, it becomes a double doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion that שמואל holds like רבי אליעזר. It says the wine case can be permitted for a different reason: it is a ספק ספיקא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the valley case from the משנה there is only one doubt: did he enter the place or not? With the thieves there are two doubts: maybe the thieves were Jews, and even if they were גוים, maybe they only wanted money and never touched the wine. Because of this double doubt, שמואל's ruling no longer depends on the view of רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; the case is not truly comparable
A double doubt: a doubt on top of a doubt, which is usually treated leniently

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל permitted the wine not because he follows רבי אליעזר, but because the wine case has two separate doubts, a ספק ספיקא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the thieves were definitely Jews or definitely after money. It is saying each possibility is unsure, and two unsure points stacked together are what make it a ספק ספיקא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ספק ספיקא can be enough to permit, so a ruling can stand without depending on a single disputed opinion.

phrases.english: No, it is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the wine barrels case that שמואל ruled on.

phrases.english: since there are those who open (barrels)
for the sake of money,
phrases.notes: Some thieves open barrels hoping to find money hidden inside, not to get at the wine itself.

phrases.english: it is a double doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison built in steps 26 and 27 between שמואל's wine case and the valley case of רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that שמואל's ruling must follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The valley case has a single doubt, but the wine case has two doubts (were the thieves Jews, and did they even touch the wine), making it a ספק ספיקא that can be permitted on its own.
